blocks.content: The Container Network Interface (CNI) is the plugin standard that actually implements the flat, direct Pod-to-Pod network model covered earlier in this module, Kubernetes itself does not ship with networking built in, it requires a CNI plugin to be installed.

CNI is the standardized interface that makes the pod networking model covered in the Pod-to-Pod Communication topic real, assigning IPs to Pods and setting up the actual routing that lets them reach each other directly.

blocks.alt: The plugin standard that turns the flat network model from theory into reality

blocks.content: When a new Pod starts, kubelet, covered in the Architecture module, calls out to the configured CNI plugin to actually set up that Pod's networking, assigning it an IP and wiring it into the cluster's network.

blocks.alt: The exact moment kubelet hands off networking setup to the CNI plugin

blocks.content: Several CNI plugins are widely used in production, Calico, Flannel, and Cilium are among the most common, each implementing the same required Pod networking model, but with different underlying approaches and additional capabilities.

blocks.alt: Several established options, all satisfying the same core requirement

blocks.content: Different CNI plugins make genuinely different tradeoffs, some prioritize raw network performance, some offer richer support for the Network Policies covered in the next topic, some add deeper observability, the right choice depends on what a specific cluster actually needs.

blocks.alt: Genuinely different strengths, not interchangeable, purely cosmetic choices

blocks.content: This is worth stating plainly: Kubernetes itself does not include a CNI plugin, a cluster without one installed cannot actually network its Pods at all, installing a CNI plugin is a required, deliberate step in setting up any cluster from scratch.

blocks.alt: A required, deliberate installation step, not something that comes for free

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: CNI is the plugin standard that actually implements Kubernetes's required flat, NAT-free Pod networking model, kubelet calls it when a new Pod starts.
Kubernetes ships with no CNI plugin built in, Calico, Flannel, and Cilium are common choices, each with genuinely different tradeoffs worth choosing deliberately.
